body.en: For years the memory of the pool haunted Douglas. Whenever he went near water, the old terror returned. It spoiled fishing trips, canoeing and swimming in the lakes and rivers he loved. He finally decided that he had to get an instructor and learn to swim properly.

title.en: How the instructor built a swimmer

narration.en: Let us list what the instructor taught and why.

say.en: First a belt on a rope over a pulley kept him safe, so he could trust the water.
Next he learnt to breathe out with his face under water.
Then to raise his nose and breathe in, building a rhythm.
Then to kick with his legs, relaxed and steady.
Finally he swam alone in lakes to test whether the fear was gone.

prompt.en: Put the steps of the training in order.

steps.en: Douglas decides to hire an instructor
A belt is put round him, tied to a rope over a pulley
He swims to and fro while the instructor holds the rope
He learns to put his face under and breathe out
He learns to raise his nose and breathe in
He learns to kick with his legs
He tests himself alone in the pool
He tests himself in lakes until the fear is gone

explanation.en: Small, steady steps, not one dramatic leap, defeated a fear that had spoiled years of his life.

body.en: The instructor put a belt around Douglas, attached to a rope that ran over a pulley, and held the end of it as he swam back and forth across the pool. Then he taught him one skill at a time: to put his face under water and breathe out, to raise his nose and breathe in, and then to kick with his legs. Piece by piece he built a swimmer. Even then, Douglas tested himself alone, first in the pool and later in lakes, until the fear was really gone.

points.en: Breathing: exhale under water, inhale above
Kicking with relaxed legs; then the whole stroke
Tested himself alone in lakes until the fear left
